# Engage: Why Does the Moon Look Different? {#mp-engage}

::: {.engage-box}
## 🌀 A Hurricane and a Full Moon

On the evening of **October 29, 2012**, Hurricane Sandy pushed the ocean into New York City. At **The Battery** (the tip of Manhattan) the water rose to **14.06 ft** above the usual lowest tide level, about **9 ft above a normal high tide** and about **4 ft higher** than the old record (Hurricane Donna, 1960). Subways, tunnels, and neighborhoods flooded.

That same afternoon, the Moon was **full**.

**Our question:** How does the Moon contribute to storm severity? To answer it, we first need to understand **why the Moon changes shape** and **how the Moon controls the tides**.
:::

When students think about how storms could get worse in the future (the Unit 5 Performance Task), it helps to know what *else* makes a storm more or less damaging, **with or without climate change**. The Moon is one of those things.

## Moon Phase Patterns {#mp-observe}

Each circle below is the Moon's shape on one day (calculated, not photos). **Tap or hover on any Moon** to see its date and phase. Change the year to compare.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
d3 = require("d3@7.9.0")
Plot = require("@observablehq/plot@0.6.16")
mpSynodic = 29.530588853
mpRefNew = Date.UTC(2000, 0, 6, 18, 14)
mpPhaseOf = t => { const days = (t - mpRefNew) / 86400000; return (((days / mpSynodic) % 1) + 1) % 1; }
mpPhaseName = p => {
  const age = p * mpSynodic;
  if (age < 1 || age > mpSynodic - 1) return "New Moon";
  if (Math.abs(age - mpSynodic / 4) < 1) return "First Quarter";
  if (Math.abs(age - mpSynodic / 2) < 1) return "Full Moon";
  if (Math.abs(age - 3 * mpSynodic / 4) < 1) return "Third Quarter";
  return p < 0.25 ? "Waxing Crescent" : p < 0.5 ? "Waxing Gibbous" : p < 0.75 ? "Waning Gibbous" : "Waning Crescent";
}
// SVG path of the lit part of a moon of radius r, as seen from the Northern Hemisphere (p = 0 new, 0.5 full)
mpMoonPath = (p, r) => {
  const waxing = p < 0.5;
  const c = Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * p);
  const rx = Math.abs(c) * r;
  const litSweep = waxing ? 1 : 0;
  const termSweep = waxing ? (c < 0 ? 1 : 0) : (c > 0 ? 1 : 0);
  return `M0,${-r} A${r},${r} 0 0 ${litSweep} 0,${r} A${rx},${r} 0 0 ${termSweep} 0,${-r}Z`;
}
mpIllum = p => (1 - Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * p)) / 2
mpSvg = s => { const d = document.createElement("div"); d.innerHTML = s; return d.firstElementChild; }
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const cell = 22, r = 8.5, left = 40, top = 24;
  const W = left + 31 * cell + 6, H = top + 12 * cell + 6;
  const monthFmt = new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", {month: "short", timeZone: "UTC"});
  const readout = html`<div style="min-height:2.6em;font-size:.95em;margin:6px 0;padding:8px 12px;border-radius:10px;background:#1e1b4b;color:#e0e7ff;">👆 Tap a Moon to see its date and phase.</div>`;
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${W} ${H}`)
    .style("width", "100%").style("height", "auto").style("background", "#0b1020")
    .style("border-radius", "12px").style("font", "10px sans-serif");
  for (let d = 1; d <= 31; d++)
    svg.append("text").attr("x", left + (d - 0.5) * cell).attr("y", top - 9).attr("text-anchor", "middle")
      .attr("fill", "#94a3b8").text(d % 5 === 0 || d === 1 ? d : "");
  for (let m = 0; m < 12; m++) {
    const y = top + (m + 0.5) * cell;
    svg.append("text").attr("x", 6).attr("y", y + 3.5).attr("fill", "#cbd5e1").text(monthFmt.format(new Date(Date.UTC(mpYear, m, 1))));
    const nDays = new Date(Date.UTC(mpYear, m + 1, 0)).getUTCDate();
    for (let d = 1; d <= nDays; d++) {
      const t = Date.UTC(mpYear, m, d, 12);
      const p = mpPhaseOf(t);
      const g = svg.append("g").attr("transform", `translate(${left + (d - 0.5) * cell},${y})`).style("cursor", "pointer");
      g.append("circle").attr("r", r + 2).attr("fill", "transparent");
      g.append("circle").attr("r", r).attr("fill", "#334155");
      g.append("path").attr("d", mpMoonPath(p, r)).attr("fill", "#f5f0d0");
      const label = `${new Date(t).toLocaleDateString("en-US", {timeZone: "UTC", dateStyle: "medium"})}: ${mpPhaseName(p)} (${Math.round(mpIllum(p) * 100)}% lit, Moon age about ${(p * mpSynodic).toFixed(1)} days)`;
      g.append("title").text(label);
      g.on("click", () => { readout.textContent = "🌙 " + label + (mpYear === 2012 && m === 9 && d === 29 ? " · Hurricane Sandy's landfall day!" : ""); });
      if (mpYear === 2012 && m === 9 && d === 29)
        g.append("circle").attr("r", r + 2.5).attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", "#f87171").attr("stroke-width", 2.2);
    }
  }
  return html`<div>${svg.node()}${readout}<p class="mp-note">Phases are calculated from the average lunar month (29.53 days), so a phase can be off by up to about a day.${mpYear === 2012 ? " The red ring marks October 29, 2012: Sandy's landfall, the same day as the full Moon (exact full Moon: 3:49 pm EDT)." : ""}</p></div>`;
}
```

# Explore 1: Observing Models of Moon Phases {#mp-explore1}

::: {.explore-box}
## 🔦 Modeling the Moon

In class you used two models to look for patterns that might show **what causes** the phases:

- a **3-D model**: a lamp (the Sun), a ball on a stick with one side marked (the Moon), and your head (Earth), in a dark room
- a **moon phase simulator**

Look for patterns. The formal explanation comes in Explain 1.
:::

## The Ball-and-Lamp Model {#mp-ball-model}

**In class:** One person holds the ball at arm's length and turns slowly in a circle (counterclockwise), while the lamp stays still. A partner watches from outside. The person holding the ball watches how much of the lit side they can see.

**Here:** The top panel is the view **from above the North Pole** (not to scale). The bottom panel is **what you see from Earth**. Drag the slider or press ▶ to move the Moon around its orbit.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof mpDay = Inputs.range([0, 29.5], {step: 0.1, value: 0, label: "Days since new Moon:"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
mpPlayBtn = {
  const b = html`<button class="mp-btn">▶ Play one lunar month</button>`;
  b.onclick = () => {
    const input = viewof mpDay;
    let t = 0;
    const timer = setInterval(() => {
      t = Math.round((t + 0.25) * 100) / 100;
      input.value = Math.min(t, 29.5);
      input.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}));
      if (t >= 29.5) clearInterval(timer);
    }, 70);
  };
  return b;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof mpShow = Inputs.checkbox(["Show Earth's shadow", "Show the Moon's marked side (always faces Earth)"], {value: ["Show the Moon's marked side (always faces Earth)"]})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const p = mpDay / mpSynodic;
  const W = 420, H = 300, cx = 250, cy = 150, R = 110, rm = 14, re = 26;
  const phi = Math.PI + 2 * Math.PI * p;           // moon angle (math convention, y up)
  const mx = cx + R * Math.cos(phi), my = cy - R * Math.sin(phi);
  const toward = Math.atan2(cy - my, cx - mx) * 180 / Math.PI; // direction from moon to Earth (screen)
  let s = `<svg viewBox="0 0 ${W} ${H}" style="width:100%;background:#0b1020;border-radius:12px;font:12px sans-serif">`;
  s += `<defs><marker id="mpArr" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="5" refY="5" markerWidth="5" markerHeight="5" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0L10,5L0,10z" fill="#fde68a"/></marker></defs>`;
  for (let k = 0; k < 6; k++) { const y = 30 + k * 48; s += `<line x1="8" y1="${y}" x2="70" y2="${y}" stroke="#fde68a" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#mpArr)" opacity=".8"/>`; }
  s += `<text x="8" y="16" fill="#fde68a" font-weight="700">☀️ Sunlight (lamp)</text>`;
  if (mpShow.includes("Show Earth's shadow")) s += `<polygon points="${cx},${cy - re} ${W},${cy - re + 8} ${W},${cy + re - 8} ${cx},${cy + re}" fill="#000" opacity=".55"/>`;
  s += `<circle cx="${cx}" cy="${cy}" r="${R}" fill="none" stroke="#475569" stroke-dasharray="4 4"/>`;
  // Earth: lit half faces left
  s += `<circle cx="${cx}" cy="${cy}" r="${re}" fill="#1e3a8a"/><path d="M${cx},${cy - re} A${re},${re} 0 0 0 ${cx},${cy + re}Z" fill="#60a5fa"/>`;
  s += `<text x="${cx}" y="${cy + re + 15}" fill="#cbd5e1" text-anchor="middle">Earth (your head)</text>`;
  // Moon: lit half faces left
  s += `<circle cx="${mx}" cy="${my}" r="${rm}" fill="#334155"/><path d="M${mx},${my - rm} A${rm},${rm} 0 0 0 ${mx},${my + rm}Z" fill="#f5f0d0"/>`;
  if (mpShow.includes("Show the Moon's marked side (always faces Earth)")) {
    const a = toward * Math.PI / 180;
    s += `<circle cx="${mx + Math.cos(a) * rm * 0.6}" cy="${my + Math.sin(a) * rm * 0.6}" r="3.5" fill="#f43f5e"/>`;
  }
  s += `<line x1="${cx}" y1="${cy}" x2="${mx}" y2="${my}" stroke="#a5b4fc" stroke-dasharray="2 3" opacity=".7"/>`;
  s += `<text x="${W - 6}" y="${H - 8}" fill="#94a3b8" text-anchor="end">Orbit: counterclockwise, viewed from above the North Pole</text>`;
  s += `</svg>`;
  const view = `<svg viewBox="-60 -60 120 120" style="width:140px;height:140px;background:#0b1020;border-radius:50%;flex:0 0 auto"><circle r="50" fill="#334155"/><path d="${mpMoonPath(p, 50)}" fill="#f5f0d0"/></svg>`;
  const angle = Math.round(360 * p);
  return html`<div class="mp-svg-wrap">${mpSvg(s)}
  <div style="display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:14px;align-items:center;margin-top:10px;">
    ${mpSvg(view)}
    <div class="mp-cards" style="flex:1 1 220px;">
      <div class="mp-card"><span class="lab">Phase seen from Earth</span><b class="big">${mpPhaseName(p)}</b></div>
      <div class="mp-card"><span class="lab">Part of the face we see that is lit</span><b class="big">${Math.round(mpIllum(p) * 100)}%</b></div>
      <div class="mp-card"><span class="lab">Angle Sun–Earth–Moon</span><b class="big">${angle > 180 ? 360 - angle : angle}°</b>${angle === 0 || angle === 360 ? "Moon toward the Sun" : angle === 180 ? "Moon opposite the Sun" : ""}</div>
    </div>
  </div></div>`;
}
```

::: {.explain-box}
## 🧠 From Patterns to an Explanation

:::

## Your Diagram Model {#mp-diagram}

Here is the top view with **8 Moon positions**. The Sun is to the left. For each position, choose the phase someone on Earth would see. Then press **Check my diagram**.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const names = ["New Moon", "Waxing Crescent", "First Quarter", "Waxing Gibbous", "Full Moon", "Waning Gibbous", "Third Quarter", "Waning Crescent"];
  const W = 360, H = 300, cx = 200, cy = 150, R = 105, rm = 13;
  let s = `<svg viewBox="0 0 ${W} ${H}" style="width:100%;max-width:520px;background:#0b1020;border-radius:12px;font:12px sans-serif">`;
  s += `<text x="8" y="18" fill="#fde68a" font-weight="700">☀️ Sun</text>`;
  for (let k = 0; k < 6; k++) { const y = 40 + k * 46; s += `<line x1="6" y1="${y}" x2="46" y2="${y}" stroke="#fde68a" stroke-width="2" opacity=".7"/>`; }
  s += `<circle cx="${cx}" cy="${cy}" r="${R}" fill="none" stroke="#475569" stroke-dasharray="4 4"/>`;
  s += `<circle cx="${cx}" cy="${cy}" r="22" fill="#1e3a8a"/><path d="M${cx},${cy - 22} A22,22 0 0 0 ${cx},${cy + 22}Z" fill="#60a5fa"/><text x="${cx}" y="${cy + 4}" text-anchor="middle" fill="#fff" font-weight="700">Earth</text>`;
  for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
    const phi = Math.PI + i * Math.PI / 4;
    const x = cx + R * Math.cos(phi), y = cy - R * Math.sin(phi);
    s += `<circle cx="${x}" cy="${y}" r="${rm}" fill="#334155"/><path d="M${x},${y - rm} A${rm},${rm} 0 0 0 ${x},${y + rm}Z" fill="#f5f0d0"/>`;
    const lx = cx + (R + 26) * Math.cos(phi), ly = cy - (R + 26) * Math.sin(phi);
    s += `<circle cx="${lx}" cy="${ly}" r="10" fill="#6366f1"/><text x="${lx}" y="${ly + 4}" text-anchor="middle" fill="#fff" font-weight="800">${i + 1}</text>`;
  }
  s += `</svg>`;
  const shuffled = names.slice().sort();
  const rows = names.map((n, i) => {
    const sel = html`<select style="min-height:40px;font-size:.95em;max-width:100%;"><option value="">Choose...</option>${shuffled.map(o => html`<option>${o}</option>`)}</select>`;
    const mark = html`<span style="margin-left:6px;font-weight:700;"></span>`;
    return {sel, mark, row: html`<div style="display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;margin:4px 0;flex-wrap:wrap;"><b style="background:#6366f1;color:#fff;border-radius:50%;width:26px;height:26px;display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;">${i + 1}</b>${sel}${mark}</div>`};
  });
  const msg = html`<div style="margin-top:8px;font-size:.95em;"></div>`;
  const btn = html`<button class="mp-btn">Check my diagram</button>`;
  btn.onclick = () => {
    let n = 0;
    rows.forEach((r, i) => {
      const ok = r.sel.value === names[i];
      if (ok) n++;
      r.mark.textContent = r.sel.value ? (ok ? "✅" : "❌") : "";
    });
    msg.innerHTML = n === 8 ? "🎉 <b>8 / 8!</b> Notice: position 1 is between Earth and the Sun (new), position 5 is opposite the Sun (full). The Sun lights the left half of the Moon at every position."
      : `<b>${n} / 8 correct.</b> Hint: imagine standing on Earth facing each Moon. How much of its lit (left) half faces you? Moon positions go counterclockwise, and the lit part grows on the right side first.`;
  };
  return html`<div class="mp-svg-wrap" style="display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:14px;align-items:flex-start;">
    <div style="flex:1 1 280px;min-width:0;">${mpSvg(s)}</div>
    <div style="flex:1 1 220px;min-width:0;">${rows.map(r => r.row)}${btn}${msg}</div></div>`;
}
```

## Lunar Phases: Text {#mp-lunar-text}

Your class read the CK-12 text [*Lunar Phases*](https://flexbooks.ck12.org/cbook/ck-12-middle-school-earth-science-flexbook-2.0/section/3.11/primary/lesson/lunar-phases-ms-es/) to gain ideas and **evaluate your diagram**. As you read, mark where the text **confirms** your model, **contradicts** it, or raises a **question**. The key points:

| Idea from the text | What it means |
|---|---|
| The Moon **does not make its own light** | We see sunlight **reflected** off the Moon |
| The Sun always lights **half** of the Moon | Like the ball in the lamp model |
| The Moon **orbits Earth** about every month | As it moves, we see **different amounts** of the lit half |
| **Waxing** = lit part growing; **waning** = shrinking | **Crescent** = less than half lit; **gibbous** = more than half lit |
| One cycle takes **29.5 days** | About one month ("moon-th") |
| The same side of the Moon **always faces Earth** | The Moon spins once for each trip around Earth |

::: {.key-idea}
**🔑 Consensus Ideas: Phases of the Moon**

- The Sun always lights **half** of the Moon.
- The Moon's **position in its orbit** around Earth determines **how much of the lit half we see** from Earth. That is the phase.
- **New Moon:** Moon between Earth and Sun (we see the dark half). **Full Moon:** Earth between Sun and Moon (we see the whole lit half). **Quarters:** Moon at a right angle to the Sun–Earth line (we see half of the lit half).
- The pattern **repeats every 29.53 days**. Phases are a **cycle**, caused by the **relative positions** of the Sun, Earth, and Moon, **not** by Earth's shadow.
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  if (!mpProbe) return html`<div class="student-task"><b>🔁 Revisit your Engage idea:</b> You didn't pick an idea at the start. Scroll up to <a href="#mp-probe">Your Initial Idea</a>, choose one, then come back.</div>`;
  const k = mpProbe[0];
  const fb = {
    A: "The models don't support this. Earth's shadow points away from the Sun, so it only lines up with the Moon near full Moon (that's a lunar eclipse, which is rare). Crescents and quarters happen when the Moon is nowhere near the shadow.",
    B: "Clouds can hide the Moon on a given night, but they can't make the same repeating 29.53-day pattern everywhere on Earth.",
    C: "The evidence supports this! The lamp always lit half the ball, and the amount of that lit half you could see depended on where the ball was in its orbit.",
    D: "The text says the Moon doesn't make its own light. We see reflected sunlight, which is why the lit side always faces the Sun.",
    E: "The Moon does spin, but exactly once per orbit, so the same side always faces Earth (remember the red dot). The \"dark side\" is just the side facing away from the Sun at that time.",
    F: "The Moon's distance from the Sun barely changes compared with the 150 million km to the Sun, and distance can't change the shape we see. Position relative to Earth and Sun does."
  }[k];
  return html`<div class="student-task"><b>🔁 Revisit your Engage idea:</b> ${mpProbe}<br><br>${fb}</div>`;
}
```

## Analyzing Your Tide Graph {#mp-tide-analysis}

::: {.student-task}
### ✏️ In your handout: *High Tides and Moon Phases*

- **Graph** the highest high tide for each day of your two-week period. Label the dates of the **moon phases** on your graph.
- When were the **highest** high tides? What was the moon phase then?
- When were the **lowest** high tides? What was the moon phase then?
- How many days are there between the **biggest** tides? How does that compare to the time between new Moon and full Moon?
- What **pattern** connects the tides to the phases of the Moon?

In class: discuss with your group, then whole-class Domino Discover.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## 🔑 Check your thinking (try it first!)

- **Highest** high tides came **1–2 days after the new Moon and the full Moon** (Oct 16: 6.32 ft; Oct 29: 5.50 ft; Nov 14: 6.34 ft).
- **Lowest** high tides came near the **quarter Moons** (Oct 8: 4.50 ft; Oct 24: 4.93 ft; Nov 6–7: 4.43 ft).
- The biggest tides are about **14–15 days apart**, the same as the time from new Moon to full Moon (half of 29.53 days). So tides follow a **cycle tied to the Moon's phases**.
- **Pattern:** biggest tides at new and full Moon (**spring tides**), smallest near quarter Moons (**neap tides**). The tide range peaks a day or two **after** the phase because the ocean takes time to respond.
:::

# Explain 2: Moon Phases, Tides, and Sandy {#mp-explain2}

::: {.explain-box}
## 🧠 Why Do Tides Follow the Moon?

Your class watched the video *Watching the Tides* and read the text *Tides* to build a diagram model connecting **moon phases** to **tides**. Then you used that model to answer: **why was Hurricane Sandy, which hit on a spring tide, so damaging?**
:::

## What Causes Tides? {#mp-tides-model}

Watch [*Watching the Tides*](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QcbN9SVkqYU) and read the CK-12 text [*Tides*](https://www.ck12.org/earth-science/tides/lesson/Tides-HS-ES/). Key ideas:

| Idea | What it means |
|---|---|
| **Gravity** from the Moon pulls on Earth's oceans | The ocean bulges toward the Moon, and also on the **opposite side** (Earth is pulled toward the Moon more than the far ocean is) |
| Earth **rotates** through the two bulges every day | Most coasts, including NYC, get **two high tides and two low tides** about every **24 hours 50 minutes** |
| The **Sun** also makes tides | The Sun is much bigger but much farther away, so its tide is a bit **less than half** as strong as the Moon's |
| **Spring tides** (new and full Moon) | Sun, Earth, and Moon **line up**. The bulges **add together**: higher high tides, lower low tides |
| **Neap tides** (quarter Moons) | The Sun and Moon pull at **right angles**. Their bulges partly **cancel**: smaller tidal range |

Move the Moon and watch the ocean bulge (blue). The Sun is to the left. **Not to scale**: the bulges are hugely exaggerated.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof mpTideDay = Inputs.range([0, 29.5], {step: 0.1, value: 0, label: "Days since new Moon:"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const p = mpTideDay / mpSynodic;
  const phiM = Math.PI + 2 * Math.PI * p, phiS = Math.PI;   // directions (math convention)
  const aM = 1, aS = 0.46;
  const W = 420, H = 300, cx = 230, cy = 150, re = 48, k = 16, R = 125;
  // ocean outline: r(psi) = base + k*[aM cos 2(psi-phiM) + aS cos 2(psi-phiS)]
  const pts = d3.range(0, 361, 3).map(deg => {
    const psi = deg * Math.PI / 180;
    const r = re + 14 + k * (aM * Math.cos(2 * (psi - phiM)) + aS * Math.cos(2 * (psi - phiS)));
    return [cx + r * Math.cos(psi), cy - r * Math.sin(psi)];
  });
  const amp = Math.hypot(aM * Math.cos(2 * phiM) + aS * Math.cos(2 * phiS), aM * Math.sin(2 * phiM) + aS * Math.sin(2 * phiS));
  const mx = cx + R * Math.cos(phiM), my = cy - R * Math.sin(phiM);
  let s = `<svg viewBox="0 0 ${W} ${H}" style="width:100%;background:#0b1020;border-radius:12px;font:12px sans-serif">`;
  s += `<text x="8" y="18" fill="#fde68a" font-weight="700">☀️ Sun's pull</text>`;
  for (let j = 0; j < 6; j++) { const y = 40 + j * 46; s += `<line x1="6" y1="${y}" x2="50" y2="${y}" stroke="#fde68a" stroke-width="2" opacity=".6"/>`; }
  s += `<circle cx="${cx}" cy="${cy}" r="${R}" fill="none" stroke="#475569" stroke-dasharray="4 4"/>`;
  s += `<path d="M${pts.map(q => q.join(",")).join("L")}Z" fill="#38bdf8" fill-opacity=".55" stroke="#7dd3fc"/>`;
  s += `<circle cx="${cx}" cy="${cy}" r="${re}" fill="#166534"/><text x="${cx}" y="${cy + 4}" text-anchor="middle" fill="#fff" font-weight="700">Earth</text>`;
  s += `<circle cx="${mx}" cy="${my}" r="13" fill="#334155"/><path d="M${mx},${my - 13} A13,13 0 0 0 ${mx},${my + 13}Z" fill="#f5f0d0"/>`;
  s += `<line x1="${cx}" y1="${cy}" x2="${mx}" y2="${my}" stroke="#c4b5fd" stroke-dasharray="3 3"/>`;
  s += `</svg>`;
  const kind = amp > 1.3 ? "Spring tide" : amp < 0.7 ? "Neap tide" : "In between";
  const color = amp > 1.3 ? "#b91c1c" : amp < 0.7 ? "#1d4ed8" : "#475569";
  return html`<div class="mp-svg-wrap">${mpSvg(s)}
  <div class="mp-cards">
    <div class="mp-card"><span class="lab">Moon phase</span><b class="big">${mpPhaseName(p)}</b></div>
    <div class="mp-card"><span class="lab">Tide type</span><b class="big" style="color:${color}">${kind}</b></div>
    <div class="mp-card"><span class="lab">Tidal bulge vs. Moon alone</span><b class="big">${Math.round(amp * 100)}%</b>Spring ≈ 146%, neap ≈ 54%</div>
  </div>
  <p class="mp-note">Model uses the ideal ratio of Sun's tide to Moon's tide (0.46). Real coastlines change the exact sizes; at The Battery in Oct 2012, spring high tides were about 1–2 ft higher than neap high tides.</p></div>`;
}
```

```{ojs}

  {
    q: "Set the Moon to full (about 14.8 days). Why is the bulge large even though the Moon is on the opposite side from the Sun?",
    options: ["The Moon is closer at full Moon", "The Sun and Moon each make bulges on both the near and far sides of Earth, so they still line up and add together", "Earth's shadow increases the tide", "Full Moons are brighter"],
    correct: 1,

  },

    q: "Set the Moon to first quarter (about 7.4 days). What happens?",
    options: ["The bulge is biggest", "The Sun's and Moon's bulges are at right angles and partly cancel: a neap tide", "There is no tide at all", "Only the Sun makes a tide"],
    correct: 1,
    explanation: "At the quarter Moons, the Moon's bulge points one way and the Sun's points at 90°. The Moon still wins, but the range is smaller. That matches the dips you saw in your tide graph."
  },
  {
    q: "About how often do spring tides happen?",
    options: ["Once a year", "Once a month", "About every 14–15 days (twice a month)", "Every day"],
    correct: 2,
    explanation: "New Moon and full Moon are each once per 29.53-day cycle, so there's a spring tide about every 14.8 days."
  }
])
```

## Why Was Sandy So Bad? {#mp-sandy}

A **storm surge** is extra water pushed toward the coast by a storm's winds (plus a small rise from low air pressure). The water level that floods the city is the **storm tide**:

<div style="text-align:center;font-size:1.15em;font-weight:700;margin:10px 0;">storm tide = normal (astronomical) tide + storm surge</div>

Below is the real record from The Battery. The **blue line** is the tide NOAA predicted from the Moon and Sun alone. The **red line** is what the water actually did.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
mpSurge = mpObs.map((v, i) => v - mpPred[i])
viewof mpShift = Inputs.range([-6, 6], {step: 1, value: 0, label: "Move the surge earlier (−) or later (+), hours:"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof mpTideKind = Inputs.radio(["Actual tide (full Moon, Oct 29)", "Neap-size tide (model)", "Extra-large spring tide like Oct 16 (model)"], {value: "Actual tide (full Moon, Oct 29)", label: "Tide:"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const MTL = 2.47;   // mean tide level, ft above MLLW
  const scale = mpTideKind.startsWith("Neap") ? 0.67 : mpTideKind.startsWith("Extra") ? 1.27 : 1;
  const tide = mpPred.map(v => MTL + (v - MTL) * scale);
  const changed = mpShift !== 0 || scale !== 1;
  const rows = mpPred.map((v, h) => {
    const j = h - mpShift;
    const s = j >= 0 && j < mpSurge.length ? mpSurge[j] : NaN;
    return {h, tide: tide[h], surge: s, storm: tide[h] + s, obs: mpObs[h]};
  }).filter(d => d.h >= 36 && d.h <= 96);
  const valid = rows.filter(d => !isNaN(d.storm));
  const peak = valid.reduce((a, b) => b.storm > a.storm ? b : a);
  const actualPeak = 14.06;
  const marks = [
    Plot.ruleY([5.05], {stroke: "#64748b", strokeDasharray: "6 4"}),
    Plot.text([{h: 37, y: 5.05}], {x: "h", y: "y", text: () => "normal high tide (MHHW 5.05 ft)", textAnchor: "start", dy: -7, fill: "currentColor", fontSize: 11}),
    Plot.areaY(valid, {x: "h", y1: 0, y2: "surge", fill: "#f97316", fillOpacity: 0.25, curve: "monotone-x"}),
    Plot.lineY(valid, {x: "h", y: "surge", stroke: "#ea580c", strokeWidth: 1.5, strokeDasharray: "3 2", curve: "monotone-x"}),
    Plot.lineY(rows, {x: "h", y: "tide", stroke: "#0284c7", strokeWidth: 2.2, curve: "monotone-x"}),
    Plot.lineY(valid, {x: "h", y: "storm", stroke: "#dc2626", strokeWidth: 3, curve: "monotone-x"}),
    Plot.dot([peak], {x: "h", y: "storm", r: 6, fill: "#dc2626", stroke: "white"}),
    Plot.text([peak], {x: "h", y: "storm", text: d => `${d.storm.toFixed(1)} ft`, dy: -14, fontWeight: 800, fill: "#dc2626"}),
    Plot.tip(rows, Plot.pointerX({x: "h", y: "storm", title: d => `${mpHourLabel(d.h)}\nTide: ${d.tide.toFixed(1)} ft\nSurge: ${isNaN(d.surge) ? "n/a" : d.surge.toFixed(1)} ft\nStorm tide: ${isNaN(d.storm) ? "n/a" : d.storm.toFixed(1)} ft`}))
  ];
  if (changed) marks.unshift(Plot.lineY(rows, {x: "h", y: "obs", stroke: "#94a3b8", strokeWidth: 1.5, curve: "monotone-x"}));
  const chart = Plot.plot({
    title: changed ? "What if? Storm tide with your changes (gray = what really happened)" : "Hurricane Sandy at The Battery, Oct 28–30, 2012",
    subtitle: "Blue = predicted tide · orange = storm surge · red = storm tide (water level)",
    width, height: 380, marginLeft: 50,
    x: {label: null, ticks: d3.range(36, 97, 12), tickFormat: h => mpHourTick(h)},
    y: {label: "Water level (ft above MLLW)", domain: [-1, 15.5], grid: true},
    marks
  });
  const peakHour = mpHourLabel(peak.h);
  return html`<div>${chart}
  <div class="mp-cards">
    <div class="mp-card"><span class="lab">Highest storm tide (this view)</span><b class="big">${peak.storm.toFixed(1)} ft</b>${peakHour} (hourly data)</div>
    <div class="mp-card"><span class="lab">Real peak (6-minute data)</span><b class="big">${actualPeak} ft</b>Oct 29, 9:24 pm EDT</div>
    <div class="mp-card"><span class="lab">Change from what really happened</span><b class="big">${changed ? (peak.storm - 13.99 >= 0 ? "+" : "") + (peak.storm - 13.99).toFixed(1) + " ft" : "0 ft"}</b>vs. hourly peak 13.99 ft</div>
  </div></div>`;
}
```

<p class="mp-note">Data: NOAA CO-OPS station 8518750, hourly water level and tide predictions (ft above MLLW, EDT). Surge = observed − predicted. "What if" options are a simple model: the surge curve is shifted in time, and the tide is scaled around mean tide level (neap-size ≈ the Oct 8 neap; extra-large ≈ the Oct 16 spring tide).</p>

::: {.callout-tip}
## 🔎 Try these

- With no changes, read the peak: about **9.3 ft of surge** on top of about **4.7 ft of tide** at 9:24 pm. The predicted high tide was at 8:48 pm, so **the surge peaked right at high tide**.
- Move the surge **6 hours** later (to low tide). How much lower is the peak?
- Switch to a **neap-size tide**. How much does the peak drop? Then try the **extra-large spring tide**.
:::

```{ojs}
    options: ["About 4.7 ft", "About 9.3 ft", "About 14 ft", "About 19 ft"],
    correct: 1,
    explanation: "Storm tide = tide + surge, so surge ≈ 14.06 − 4.7 ≈ 9.3 ft. NOAA measured a peak surge of about 9.3–9.4 ft. The water was about 9 ft above a normal high tide (MHHW, 5.05 ft)."
  },
  {

    options: ["It goes up", "It drops by several feet, because the surge is now added to low water instead of high water", "It doesn't change", "The surge disappears"],
    correct: 1,

  },

    q: "Which statement best explains how the Moon contributed to Sandy's flooding?",
    options: ["The full Moon caused the hurricane", "The full Moon made a spring tide, so the high tide that the surge arrived on was higher than it would be at a neap tide", "The Moon's light heated the ocean", "The Moon pulled the hurricane toward NYC"],
    correct: 1,
    explanation: "The Moon didn't create the storm or steer it. It set the baseline: Sandy's surge arrived at high tide during a spring tide. With a neap tide the water would have been roughly a foot lower, and with an extra-large spring tide even higher."
  }
```

::: {.student-task}
### ✏️ In your handout: *Why was Hurricane Sandy so Bad?*

Use the video, the text *Tides*, and your tide graph to answer: **Why was Hurricane Sandy, which hit on a spring tide, so damaging?**

- Draw a **diagram model** showing the positions of the Sun, Earth, and Moon on **October 29, 2012**, and the tidal bulges.
- Explain how the **moon phase** connects to the **height of the tide**.
- Explain how the **tide** and the **storm surge** combined to make the flooding.

In class: Think-Talk-Open Exchange in groups of three, then **revise** your response.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## 🔑 Check your thinking (try it first!)

- **Diagram:** Sun, Earth, and Moon in a **line**, with Earth between the Sun and the **full Moon**. Tidal bulges from the Sun and Moon line up and **add together**.
- **Phase → tide:** At new and full Moon, the Sun's and Moon's gravity pull along the same line, making **spring tides** (higher high tides). At quarter Moons they're at right angles, making **neap tides**.
- **Sandy:** Sandy's winds pushed a **storm surge of about 9 ft** toward New York Harbor. It arrived at about the time of the evening **high tide**, during a **full-Moon spring tide**. Storm tide = tide + surge, so the water reached a record **14.06 ft above MLLW** (about 9 ft above normal high tide) at 9:24 pm EDT.
- **Conclusion:** The Moon didn't cause the storm, but its position **raised the starting water level**. A storm's severity depends on **when** it arrives (tide timing and phase), not just how strong it is.
:::

::: {.key-idea}
**🔑 Consensus Ideas: Moon Phases and Tides**

- The **Moon's gravity** (and, less, the **Sun's**) makes tidal bulges; Earth's rotation gives most coasts **two high and two low tides** a day.
- **Spring tides** happen at **new and full Moon**, when the Sun, Earth, and Moon line up. **Neap tides** happen at the **quarter Moons**.
- Tides follow the Moon's **29.53-day cycle**, with two spring tides and two neap tides per cycle.
- A storm surge that arrives at **high tide during a spring tide** causes the **worst flooding**. That's what happened during Sandy.
:::

# Elaborate: What Causes Lunar and Solar Eclipses? {#mp-eclipses}

::: {.elaborate-box}
## 🌒 One More Moon Pattern

If the Moon is between Earth and the Sun **every** new Moon, and Earth is between the Sun and Moon **every** full Moon, why don't we get an eclipse **every month**? Your class read the text [*Eclipses*](https://flexbooks.ck12.org/cbook/ck-12-middle-school-earth-science-flexbook-2.0/section/3.8/primary/lesson/eclipses-hs-es/) and used Read-Generate-Sort-Solve to figure it out.
:::

| | Solar eclipse | Lunar eclipse |
|---|---|---|
| **Moon phase** | **New Moon** | **Full Moon** |
| **What lines up** | Sun → **Moon** → Earth | Sun → **Earth** → Moon |
| **Whose shadow?** | The **Moon's** shadow falls on Earth | **Earth's** shadow falls on the Moon |
| **Who can see it** | Only people in the narrow shadow path | Everyone on the night side of Earth |
| **Real example** | **Nov 13, 2012** total solar eclipse (northern Australia), just 15 days after Sandy | **Nov 28, 2012** penumbral (faint) lunar eclipse |

**The key:** the Moon's orbit is **tilted about 5°** compared with Earth's orbit around the Sun. Most months the Moon passes **above or below** the shadow. Eclipses only happen when a new or full Moon occurs near the two places where the orbits cross (the **nodes**). That lines up about every **6 months** ("eclipse seasons").

This side view (tilt hugely exaggerated) shows the Moon at new or full Moon. Change how long it's been since an eclipse season.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof mpEclPhase = Inputs.radio(["New Moon", "Full Moon"], {value: "New Moon", label: "Phase:"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof mpEclMonths = Inputs.range([0, 12], {step: 0.5, value: 0, label: "Months since an eclipse season:"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  // Sun's angle from the node line advances 360° per eclipse year (346.62 days)
  const lam = 2 * Math.PI * (mpEclMonths * mpSynodic) / 346.62;
  const beta = 5.14 * Math.sin(lam);           // Moon's distance above/below Earth's orbital plane (degrees)
  const solar = mpEclPhase === "New Moon";
  const limit = solar ? 1.5 : 1.0;
  const ecl = Math.abs(beta) < limit;
  const W = 420, H = 220, cy = 110, mx = solar ? 210 : 330;
  const earthX = solar ? 330 : 210;
  const dy = -beta * 14;
  let s = `<svg viewBox="0 0 ${W} ${H}" style="width:100%;background:#0b1020;border-radius:12px;font:12px sans-serif">`;
  s += `<circle cx="20" cy="${cy}" r="40" fill="#fbbf24"/><text x="20" y="${cy + 58}" fill="#fde68a" text-anchor="middle">Sun</text>`;
  s += `<line x1="0" y1="${cy}" x2="${W}" y2="${cy}" stroke="#475569" stroke-dasharray="4 4"/>`;
  s += `<text x="66" y="${cy + 16}" fill="#94a3b8">plane of Earth's orbit</text>`;
  if (solar) {
    s += `<polygon points="${mx},${cy + dy - 9} ${W},${cy + dy - 3} ${W},${cy + dy + 3} ${mx},${cy + dy + 9}" fill="#000" opacity=".6"/>`;
    s += `<circle cx="${earthX}" cy="${cy}" r="24" fill="#2563eb"/><text x="${earthX}" y="${cy + 42}" fill="#cbd5e1" text-anchor="middle">Earth</text>`;
    s += `<circle cx="${mx}" cy="${cy + dy}" r="9" fill="#e2e8f0"/><text x="${mx}" y="${cy + dy - 14}" fill="#e2e8f0" text-anchor="middle">Moon</text>`;
  } else {
    s += `<polygon points="${earthX},${cy - 24} ${W},${cy - 14} ${W},${cy + 14} ${earthX},${cy + 24}" fill="#000" opacity=".6"/>`;
    s += `<circle cx="${earthX}" cy="${cy}" r="24" fill="#2563eb"/><text x="${earthX}" y="${cy + 42}" fill="#cbd5e1" text-anchor="middle">Earth</text>`;
    s += `<circle cx="${mx}" cy="${cy + dy}" r="9" fill="${ecl ? "#b45309" : "#e2e8f0"}"/><text x="${mx}" y="${cy + dy - 14}" fill="#e2e8f0" text-anchor="middle">Moon</text>`;
  }
  s += `</svg>`;
  const result = ecl ? (solar ? "🌑 Solar eclipse! The Moon's shadow reaches Earth." : "🌕 Lunar eclipse! The Moon passes through Earth's shadow.")
                     : (solar ? "No eclipse: the Moon's shadow passes above or below Earth." : "No eclipse: the full Moon passes above or below Earth's shadow.");
  return html`<div class="mp-svg-wrap">${mpSvg(s)}
  <div class="mp-cards">
    <div class="mp-card"><span class="lab">Moon above/below Earth's orbital plane</span><b class="big">${beta >= 0 ? "+" : ""}${beta.toFixed(1)}°</b>(max ±5.1°)</div>
    <div class="mp-card" style="flex:2 1 220px;"><span class="lab">Result</span><b class="big" style="font-size:1.1em;color:${ecl ? "#b91c1c" : "#0f172a"}">${result}</b></div>
  </div>
  <p class="mp-note">Simplified model. Eclipse if the Moon is within about 1.5° (solar) or 1.0° (lunar, partial or total) of the plane. Tilt drawn about 14× too big so you can see it.</p></div>`;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
mpQuiz("mp-eclipse-quiz", "Check Your Understanding: Eclipses", [
  {
    q: "Why isn't there a solar eclipse at every new Moon?",
    options: ["The Moon is too small", "The Moon's orbit is tilted about 5°, so most new Moons pass above or below the line between the Sun and Earth", "The Sun is too bright", "Solar eclipses only happen at full Moon"],
    correct: 1,
    explanation: "The tilt means the Moon's shadow usually misses Earth. Only when a new Moon happens near a node (an eclipse season, about every 6 months) does the shadow land on Earth."
  },
  {
    q: "There was a total solar eclipse on November 13, 2012. What phase was the Moon on November 28, 2012, when a faint lunar eclipse happened?",
    options: ["New Moon", "First Quarter", "Full Moon", "Third Quarter"],
    correct: 2,
    explanation: "Lunar eclipses happen only at full Moon. Half a lunar month (about 15 days) after a solar eclipse, the full Moon is still close to the node, so a lunar eclipse often follows."
  },
  {
    q: "Which phenomena from this chapter are cycles caused by the positions of the Sun, Earth, and Moon?",
    options: ["Only moon phases", "Moon phases, spring/neap tides, and eclipses", "Only hurricanes", "Only eclipses"],
    correct: 1,
    explanation: "That's the big idea of HS-ESS1-7: phases, tides, and eclipses all change in repeating cycles because of the relative positions of the Moon in its orbit, Earth, and the Sun."
  }
])
```

::: {.student-task}
### ✏️ In your handout: *What Causes Lunar and Solar Eclipses?*

- **Read** the text *Eclipses*. **Generate** ideas about what causes each type of eclipse.
- **Sort** your ideas: solar eclipse vs. lunar eclipse (phase, positions, whose shadow).
- **Solve:** Draw diagram models of a solar eclipse and a lunar eclipse. Explain **why eclipses don't happen every month**.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## 🔑 Check your thinking (try it first!)

- **Solar eclipse:** new Moon; Sun–Moon–Earth in a line; the Moon's shadow falls on a small part of Earth.
- **Lunar eclipse:** full Moon; Sun–Earth–Moon in a line; Earth's shadow falls on the Moon, which can turn coppery red.
- **Not every month:** the Moon's orbit is tilted about **5°**, so the three bodies only line up exactly when a new or full Moon happens near a **node**. That happens in **eclipse seasons** about every 6 months.
- This also shows that **Earth's shadow does not cause phases**: when it does hit the Moon, we call it an eclipse, and it only happens at full Moon.
:::

There is **no Evaluate** in this 3E. Use the summary, Myth or Fact, and quiz below to check yourself.

# Looking Ahead: From the Moon to Blizzards {#mp-bridge}

::: {.elaborate-box}
## ❄️ Bridge to Blizzards

The Moon showed us that a storm's damage depends on **more than the storm itself**. A surge that arrives at **high tide** during a **spring tide** does more damage than the same surge at low tide. That's true **with or without** climate change.

Winter storms can do the same thing. On **January 4, 2018**, a powerful winter storm's surge arrived near high tide just after a full Moon, and Boston Harbor reached a **record 15.16 ft above MLLW**.

For the Performance Task, you'll argue how storms will change as global temperatures rise. Keep two kinds of factors in mind:

| Factors that change from storm to storm | Factors climate change may shift over time |
|---|---|
| Tide and moon phase when the storm hits | Ocean and air temperature |
| The storm's track and speed | Amount of water vapor in the air |
| Time of day and location | Sea level (higher starting water for every tide) |
:::

**Up next:** In [Blizzards](unit5-blizzards.qmd), you'll investigate how winter storms form and what conditions make them more severe.

# Chapter Summary

| Key Concept | Details |
|---|---|
| **Moon phases** | The Sun always lights half the Moon. The phase is how much of that lit half we see from Earth |
| **Cause** | The Moon's **position in its orbit** relative to the Sun and Earth. **Not** Earth's shadow |
| **Lunar cycle** | New → waxing crescent → first quarter → waxing gibbous → full → waning gibbous → third quarter → waning crescent → new, every **29.53 days** |
| **Tides** | Moon's gravity (and the Sun's, a bit less than half as strong) makes two bulges; NYC gets two high and two low tides about every 24 h 50 min |
| **Spring tides** | New and full Moon; Sun, Earth, Moon in a line; bulges add; biggest tidal range |
| **Neap tides** | Quarter Moons; Sun and Moon at right angles; smallest tidal range |
| **Real data** | At The Battery, Oct 2012: spring high tides about 5.5–6.3 ft, neap high tides about 4.5–4.9 ft (above MLLW) |
| **Storm tide** | Storm tide = tide + storm surge |
| **Sandy** | Full Moon Oct 29, 2012 (3:49 pm EDT). Surge about 9.3 ft arrived near high tide; record 14.06 ft above MLLW at 9:24 pm EDT, about 9 ft above normal high tide |
| **Eclipses** | Solar at new Moon, lunar at full Moon; rare because the Moon's orbit is tilted about 5° |
| **Big idea** | Phases, tides, and eclipses are **cycles** caused by Sun–Earth–Moon positions, and they affect how severe a storm's flooding is |

# Myth or Fact?

```{=html}
<div id="mp-myths" style="background:linear-gradient(135deg,#0b1020 0%,#1e1b4b 55%,#164e63 100%); color:white; padding:30px; border-radius:16px; margin:30px 0; font-family:'Inter',sans-serif; box-shadow:0 20px 60px rgba(0,0,0,0.3);">

    <div style="font-size:2.5em; margin-bottom:10px;">🎉</div>

    <button onclick="mpmfRestart()" style="margin-top:12px; min-height:44px; padding:10px 24px; border:2px solid #fbbf24; border-radius:20px; background:transparent; color:#fbbf24; font-size:0.9em; cursor:pointer; font-weight:600;">Play Again</button>
  </div>
</div>
<script>
(function() {
  var cards = [
    { text: "Moon phases are caused by Earth's shadow covering part of the Moon.", type: "Myth",
      explanation: "Earth's shadow points away from the Sun, so it can only reach the Moon at full Moon. When it does, that's a lunar eclipse. Phases happen because we see different amounts of the Moon's sunlit half as it orbits Earth." },
    { text: "The Sun always lights half of the Moon, even during a new Moon.", type: "Fact",
      explanation: "At new Moon, the lit half faces the Sun and away from us, so we see the dark half. The far side is fully sunlit then." },
    { text: "The Moon has a permanent 'dark side' that never gets sunlight.", type: "Myth",
      explanation: "There is a far side we never see from Earth (the Moon always shows us the same face), but it gets sunlight like the rest of the Moon. It's fully lit at new Moon." },
    { text: "A full cycle of Moon phases takes about 29.5 days.", type: "Fact",
      explanation: "The synodic month is 29.53 days: the time for the Moon to return to the same position relative to the Sun and Earth." },
    { text: "Spring tides only happen in the spring season.", type: "Myth",
      explanation: "'Spring' here means the water 'springs up.' Spring tides happen about twice a month, at every new and full Moon, all year long. Sandy hit on a spring tide in October." },
    { text: "There are high tides on both the side of Earth facing the Moon and the side facing away.", type: "Fact",
      explanation: "The Moon pulls the near ocean more than Earth's center, and Earth's center more than the far ocean, so the ocean bulges on both sides. That's why most coasts get two high tides a day." },
    { text: "The full Moon caused Hurricane Sandy.", type: "Myth",
      explanation: "Hurricanes form from warm ocean water and atmospheric conditions. The full Moon only made the tide higher, so Sandy's surge started from higher water." },
    { text: "The same storm surge does more damage if it arrives at high tide than at low tide.", type: "Fact",
      explanation: "Storm tide = tide + surge. At The Battery, high and low tides differ by about 4.5–5 ft, so timing alone can change the peak water level by several feet." }
  ];
  var idx = 0, score = 0, answered = 0, cardAnswered = false;
  function el(id) { return document.getElementById(id); }
  function updateCard() {
    if (idx >= cards.length) {
      ['mpmf-card','mpmf-myth','mpmf-fact','mpmf-feedback','mpmf-next'].forEach(function(i){ el(i).style.display = 'none'; });
      el('mpmf-done').style.display = 'block';
      el('mpmf-final').textContent = score;
      el('mpmf-count').textContent = cards.length;
      return;
    }
    el('mpmf-card').textContent = cards[idx].text;
    el('mpmf-progress').textContent = 'Card ' + (idx + 1) + ' of ' + cards.length;
    el('mpmf-feedback').style.display = 'none';
    el('mpmf-next').style.display = 'none';
    el('mpmf-myth').disabled = false; el('mpmf-fact').disabled = false;
    el('mpmf-myth').style.opacity = '1'; el('mpmf-fact').style.opacity = '1';
    cardAnswered = false;
  }
  window.mpmfAnswer = function(choice) {
    if (cardAnswered) return;
    cardAnswered = true; answered++;
    var card = cards[idx], correct = (choice === card.type);
    if (correct) score++;
    el('mpmf-score').textContent = score; el('mpmf-total').textContent = answered;
    var fb = el('mpmf-feedback');
    fb.style.display = 'block';
    fb.style.background = correct ? 'rgba(0,184,148,0.2)' : 'rgba(214,48,49,0.2)';
    fb.style.border = '1px solid ' + (correct ? '#00b894' : '#e17055');
    fb.innerHTML = '<strong>' + (correct ? '✅ Correct! ' : '❌ That\'s a ' + card.type + '! ') + '</strong>' + card.explanation;
    el('mpmf-myth').disabled = true; el('mpmf-fact').disabled = true;
    el('mpmf-myth').style.opacity = (choice === 'Myth') ? '1' : '0.5';
    el('mpmf-fact').style.opacity = (choice === 'Fact') ? '1' : '0.5';
    el('mpmf-next').style.display = 'block';
  };
  window.mpmfNext = function() { idx++; updateCard(); };
  window.mpmfRestart = function() {
    idx = 0; score = 0; answered = 0;
    el('mpmf-card').style.display = 'flex'; el('mpmf-myth').style.display = 'block'; el('mpmf-fact').style.display = 'block';
    el('mpmf-done').style.display = 'none'; el('mpmf-score').textContent = '0'; el('mpmf-total').textContent = '0';
    updateCard();
  };
  updateCard();
})();
</script>
```

# End-of-Chapter Quiz {#end-of-chapter-quiz}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
function buildMpQuiz(id, title, questions) {
  const outer = html`<div id="${id}" style="font-family:'Inter',sans-serif; max-width:720px; margin:18px auto;"></div>`;
  const header = html`<div style="background:linear-gradient(135deg,#4338ca 0%,#0e7490 100%);color:#fff;border-radius:14px 14px 0 0;padding:18px 24px;">
    <div style="font-size:1.1em;font-weight:700;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;"><span style="font-size:1.2em;">📝</span> ${title}</div>
    <div style="font-size:0.85em;opacity:0.9;margin-top:4px;">Select an answer for each question.</div>
  </div>`;
  const body = html`<div style="border:1.5px solid #a5b4fc;border-top:none;border-radius:0 0 14px 14px;overflow:hidden;background:#eef2ff;padding:16px;"></div>`;
  questions.forEach((qq, qi) => {
    const card = document.createElement("div");
    card.className = "mp-qcard";
    card.style.cssText = "background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;border-radius:12px;padding:16px 20px;margin-bottom:14px;box-shadow:0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.08);";
    card.innerHTML = `<p style="font-weight:700;margin:0 0 10px;color:#1e1b4b;">${qi+1}. ${qq.q}</p>`;
    const fb = document.createElement("div");
    fb.className = "mp-fb";
    fb.style.cssText = "border-radius:8px;font-size:.9em;";
    qq.options.forEach((opt, oi) => {
      const btn = document.createElement("button");
      btn.textContent = opt;
      btn.style.cssText = "display:block;width:100%;min-height:44px;text-align:left;padding:10px 14px;margin:6px 0;border:2px solid #e2e8f0;border-radius:8px;background:#fff;color:#1e1b4b;cursor:pointer;font-size:.95em;";
      btn.onclick = () => {
        if (card.dataset.answered) return;
        card.dataset.answered = "true";
        card.querySelectorAll("button").forEach(b => { b.style.cursor = "default"; b.style.color = "#475569"; });
        const right = card.querySelectorAll("button")[qq.correct];
        right.style.borderColor = "#48bb78"; right.style.background = "#f0fff4"; right.style.color = "#276749"; right.style.fontWeight = "700";
        if (oi === qq.correct) {
          fb.innerHTML = "✅ Correct! " + qq.explanation; fb.style.color = "#276749"; fb.style.background = "#f0fff4";
        } else {
          btn.style.borderColor = "#fc8181"; btn.style.background = "#fff5f5"; btn.style.color = "#9b2c2c"; btn.style.fontWeight = "700";
          fb.innerHTML = "❌ " + qq.explanation; fb.style.color = "#9b2c2c"; fb.style.background = "#fff5f5";
        }
        fb.style.padding = "10px 14px"; fb.style.marginTop = "8px";
      };
      card.appendChild(btn);
    });
    card.appendChild(fb);
    body.appendChild(card);
  });
  outer.appendChild(header);
  outer.appendChild(body);
  return outer;
}
```

```{ojs}
    correct: 0,
    explanation: "Oct 15 and Nov 13 were new Moons and Oct 29 was full. Spring tides follow each new and full Moon, about every 14.8 days."
  },

    options: ["The Moon is farther from Earth", "The Sun's and Moon's tidal pulls act at right angles and partly cancel", "The Moon stops pulling", "Earth stops rotating"],
    correct: 1,
    explanation: "This is a neap tide. The Moon's bulge and the Sun's bulge point 90° apart, so the high tides are lower and the low tides are higher."
  },
  {
    q: "At Sandy's peak, the predicted tide at The Battery was about 4.7 ft and the water reached 14.06 ft (above MLLW). If the same surge had arrived at low tide (about 0.2 ft), about how high would the water have reached?",
    options: ["About 4.7 ft", "About 9.5 ft", "About 14 ft", "About 18.8 ft"],
    correct: 1,
    explanation: "Surge ≈ 14.06 − 4.7 ≈ 9.3 ft. At low tide: 0.2 + 9.3 ≈ 9.5 ft. Still a bad flood, but about 4.5 ft lower than what happened. Timing with the tide matters a lot."
  },
  {
    q: "Which statement correctly describes the Sun–Earth–Moon positions on October 29, 2012?",
    options: ["Moon between Earth and Sun (new Moon)", "Earth between Sun and Moon, in a nearly straight line (full Moon, spring tide)", "Moon at a right angle to the Sun (neap tide)", "Sun between Earth and Moon"],
    correct: 1,
    explanation: "It was a full Moon: the three were roughly in a line with Earth in the middle, so the Sun's and Moon's tides added together."
  },
  {
    q: "The Oct 29 spring tide (about 5.5 ft) was lower than the Oct 16 spring tide (about 6.3 ft). What is the best explanation?",
    options: ["Full Moons never make spring tides", "On Oct 29 the Moon was near the farthest point of its oval orbit, so its tidal pull was weaker", "The Sun was dimmer on Oct 29", "Hurricane Sandy lowered the predicted tide"],
    correct: 1,
    explanation: "The Moon was about 403,000 km away on Oct 29 vs. about 361,000 km on Oct 17. A closer Moon pulls harder and makes bigger tides. Predicted tides are calculated from the Moon and Sun only, not storms."
  },
  {
    q: "Why do eclipses NOT happen every month?",
    options: ["The Moon's orbit is tilted about 5°, so the Sun, Earth, and Moon only line up exactly a few times a year", "The Moon stops orbiting", "Clouds block them", "The Sun moves around Earth"],
    correct: 0,
    explanation: "Most new and full Moons pass just above or below the Sun–Earth line. Eclipses happen only near the nodes, in eclipse seasons about 6 months apart."
  },

    options: ["When it arrives at low tide during a neap tide", "When it arrives at high tide during a spring tide (new or full Moon)", "Only when it arrives at night", "The Moon has no effect"],
    correct: 1,
    explanation: "Storm tide = tide + surge. The highest starting water comes at high tide near new or full Moon (especially when the Moon is close to Earth). Sea level rise adds to every tide too, a link to the Performance Task."

])
```
